messages:
Maria K.: Quick heads-up — I pushed a small runtime tweak to the canary fleet for rw-mid-v2 at 10:30 PT. Early numbers look promising: p50 ~ -9ms, p95 ~ -60ms, p99 ~ -140ms on canary traffic. Cost estimates from the bench show ~11% token-cost reduction for this workload.

deploy-bot: canary deploy 1/5 -> us-west-2 cluster started at 10:31:05 by maria.k; image: runtime:v2026.3.14-prefetch-kv1

Joel T.: Nice! What did you change?

Maria K.: Short version: tuned prefetch windows and relaxed aggressive kv-eviction heuristics for short-prefix hits. Also adjusted microbatcher min_batch to 2 for this model class and reduced eager_flush interval for multi-turns. No model changes.

Maria K.: Config snippet we used in the canary (for reference):
```
model: rw-mid-v2
kv_prefetch_frac: 0.12
eager_flush_ms: 8
microbatch_min_size: 2
kv_eviction_short_prefix_threshold: 48
```

Raj P.: Any quality regressions on eval sets?

Maria K.: Ran the usual regressions: 1M synthetic tokens + 10k evaluator prompts. Delta in token-level perplexity: +0.02 (noise). Human eval spot checks (50 prompts) show no meaningful diff. Also verified there are no differing completion tokens for deterministic prompts used in our CI.

Joel T.: Do we have concrete latency numbers from the perf harness?

Maria K.: Yes — benchmark harness (same traffic mix as customer X) shows: p50 42ms -> 33ms, p95 220ms -> 160ms, p99 452ms -> 312ms. Production canary traces match within ~5%. We pushed some example spans to Sentry for quick inspection.

Sophie L.: What about failure modes? Any increase in error rates or tail-CPU spikes?

Maria K.: No error-rate bump on canary so far. CPU was flat; GPU util slightly higher (~3%) because more requests completed faster (shorter tails). We added a short-circuit: if p99 > baseline_p99 * 1.10 OR error_rate > 0.5% over a 5m window, the rollout will automatically rollback.

Maria K.: Rolling plan: 1/5 -> 2/5 -> 50% over next 6h -> full in 24h if metrics hold. Monitoring query for the alert (promql):
```
100 * sum(rate(errors_total[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total[5m]))
```
and p99 query: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le))`

Joel T.: 👍 please also add the canary dashboard to the runtime snapshot channel.

Maria K.: Done — I posted the dashboard link in #eng-runtime-snapshots.

Raj P.: If this stays stable, could be a nice cost saver for dedicated pools too. Worth doing a longer soak on a lower-traffic dedicated pool before we apply there.

Maria K.: Agreed. I'll schedule a 48h soak on a single-dedicated pool after the prod canary completes.

Sophie L.: Nice win — big thanks to the runtime and infra teams. :tada:

Joel T.: :clap:

Maria K.: Will post a short blurb on the weekly eng-update once the 24h metrics are green.
